security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, and Next.js documentation examples. No prompt injection, credential access, malicious network behavior, command injection, or hidden execution intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger many static command-execution detections.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that shell commands are optional manual checks and should be reviewed before running in user projects.

remediation.issue: Example network URLs may look like real endpoints to automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep example.com and localhost placeholders, and avoid adding real analytics or API endpoints to the skill text.

content.value_statement: Next.js applications can become slow through large bundles, weak caching, and unoptimized media. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused performance improvements for production apps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Next.js version, App Router usage, and Pages Router indicators.
Identifies rendering strategy improvements for Server Components, Client Components, SSG, and ISR.
Recommends image, font, caching, metadata, and production configuration improvements.
Finds bundle-size opportunities with dynamic imports and more specific imports.
Produces a structured optimization report with issues, fixes, impact estimates, and next steps.
limitations: It provides guidance and edits, but real performance gains require running builds and measurements.
It focuses on Next.js 15 and App Router patterns, so older apps may need adaptation.
It cannot guarantee perfect Lighthouse scores across devices, networks, and production infrastructure.
It depends on project access and available tooling to inspect files or run audits.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Next.js app for launch
use_cases.description: Audit a production candidate for image, font, caching, metadata, and build configuration issues before release.

use_cases.title: Improve Core Web Vitals
use_cases.description: Find changes that can improve LCP, FID, and CLS through rendering, media, and script loading choices.

use_cases.title: Reduce client bundle size
use_cases.description: Identify large components, unnecessary client boundaries, and imports that increase JavaScript sent to users.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic performance audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js optimization skill to review this app for image, font, metadata, and caching issues. Give me the top fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Core Web Vitals
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the main routes for LCP, FID, and CLS problems. Suggest changes that are likely to improve Lighthouse performance scores.

prompt_templates.title: Review App Router rendering choices
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve server and client component boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the App Router pages and components. Find unnecessary client components, missing Suspense boundaries, and better static or dynamic rendering choices.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a production optimization plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production optimization report for this Next.js 15 app. Include bundle size risks, cache strategy, image and font fixes, SEO metadata, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review my Next.js app before launch.
output: Current status: App Router is present, but several routes use client components too broadly.
Issues found: unoptimized image usage, missing OpenGraph metadata, and no verified Lighthouse baseline.
Next steps: replace image usage, narrow client boundaries, add metadata, then run a production build and Lighthouse check.

output_examples.input: Help improve LCP on the home page.
output: The likely LCP candidate is the hero image.
Recommended changes: use the Next.js Image component, set dimensions, add priority, and avoid blocking scripts above the fold.
Validation: run Lighthouse after a production build and compare LCP before and after.

output_examples.input: Find bundle size problems in this app.
output: The review focuses on large components, broad imports, and unnecessary client-side rendering.
Expected output includes risky files, why they increase JavaScript, and safer split or import options.

best_practices: Measure performance before and after changes with a production build.
Prefer Server Components unless interactivity or browser APIs require a Client Component.
Optimize the largest user-visible page elements before minor improvements.
anti_patterns: Do not convert whole layouts to Client Components without a clear browser-only need.
Do not claim Core Web Vitals improvements without running a real measurement tool.
Do not add caching rules without understanding freshness requirements for each route.

faq.question: Does this skill only work with Next.js 15?
faq.answer: It is written for Next.js 15 and App Router patterns. Many recommendations also apply to Next.js 13 and 14.

faq.question: Can it automatically improve Lighthouse scores?
faq.answer: It can recommend and apply likely improvements. Final scores depend on measurement, hosting, content, and third-party scripts.

faq.question: Does it support Pages Router projects?
faq.answer: It can detect Pages Router usage and suggest migration considerations. Its strongest guidance targets App Router projects.

faq.question: Will it run external tools?
faq.answer: The skill suggests standard commands such as builds, bundle analysis, and Lighthouse. Users should approve commands before execution.

faq.question: What performance areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers rendering strategy, images, fonts, data fetching, caching, bundle size, metadata, and Core Web Vitals.

faq.question: Can teams use it before every release?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful as a release checklist, especially when paired with build checks and Lighthouse measurements.
